principle: Capability is multidimensional: correctness alone cannot close a benchmark.

required_dimensions.correctness: Task acceptance quality under the benchmark's defined rubric.
required_dimensions.latency: Time from task-ready to accepted result, with separately recorded time-to-first-useful-result when applicable.
required_dimensions.throughput: Accepted tasks or benchmark units completed per unit of wall-clock time under defined concurrency.
required_dimensions.resource_efficiency: CPU, memory, storage, network, and accelerator use required for accepted work where measurable.
required_dimensions.model_efficiency: Quality achieved per model token, inference step, model call, or equivalent measurable unit.
required_dimensions.tool_efficiency: Useful work per tool invocation and unnecessary-call rate.
required_dimensions.cost_efficiency: Measured execution cost per accepted task when cost data is available; never invent cost estimates as measured evidence.
required_dimensions.reliability: Success rate, retry rate, timeout rate, crash rate, and reproducibility across repeated runs.
required_dimensions.parallel_efficiency: Speedup and utilization relative to a documented serial or baseline execution where parallelism is applicable.
required_dimensions.recovery_efficiency: Time and resources required to recover from supported failures.
required_dimensions.regression_safety: Whether speed/resource improvements preserve correctness and dependent-suite results.

scoring: Report dimension scores separately before any composite score. Composite scores must expose weights and may not hide a critical correctness or safety failure.

gates.correctness_gate: A faster incorrect result is not a pass.
gates.safety_gate: A faster unsafe result is not a pass.
gates.reproducibility_gate: Performance claims require repeatable measurement within the benchmark's defined variance policy.
gates.regression_gate: A performance optimization that causes a required dependent regression cannot be promoted as an overall improvement.

public_pages: Show correctness, latency, throughput, resource efficiency, reliability, cost where measured, and trend data separately. Clearly label estimates, measurements, assisted execution, and unavailable dimensions.
mastery: Mastery requires acceptance on the benchmark's correctness criteria plus its applicable performance/reliability requirements; performance alone cannot compensate for correctness failure.
